name: Block Rotator
tagline: A reverb that breathes, mutates, and orbits
summary: A feedback delay network reverb built on an 8-channel diffusion core, with ten proprietary spatial algorithms, pitch-shifting tails, and an automated parameter-morphing crossfader.

highlights.title: 8-Channel Diffusion Delay Feedback Network
highlights.body: Eight parallel delay lines feed a diffusion matrix, producing dense, evolving reverb tails that range from tight ambience to vast, disintegrating spaces.

highlights.title: 10 Proprietary Spatial Algorithms
highlights.body: Two banks of five. Max Diffusion — Cyclops, Apshai, EyeDescent, Scarab, DeathIbis — scatters signal across the spectrum into lush washes. Max Rotation — BlockRotate, Schistdisc, BloodLoom, Sekhmetal, Uncoiling — builds orbiting, spiralling stereo fields with real physical motion.

highlights.title: Pitch-Shifting Reverb Tails
highlights.body: Transpose the feedback path so repeats drift upward or downward, producing shimmering, endlessly ascending spaces or subterranean descents.

highlights.title: Resonant Multi-Mode Filter
highlights.body: Shape the feedback path with a resonant filter, sculpting the tone of every repetition as it decays.

highlights.title: Parameter Morphing Crossfader
highlights.body: Capture two complete parameter states and crossfade between them — manually, via LFO, or under host automation — for transitions no single knob can produce.

highlights.title: Real-Time Visualization
highlights.body: Watch the network work: live displays of the diffusion field, stereo correlation, and level metering.

specs: Parameter morphing crossfader, LFO, host automation
Factory banks plus unlimited user presets
requirements: A DAW that supports VST3 plugins (or AU on macOS)
macOS (Intel or Apple Silicon), Windows, or Linux
Multi-core CPU recommended when visualization is enabled
audience: Producers and sound designers who want a reverb with character and motion rather than a neutral room — electronic, experimental, ambient, and cinematic work.
